advances: Identifies the endpoint slope infimum exactly with a measurable vertex-cover number of the same-index pullback set, including every constant-affine exception.  It also proves the exact quantifier equivalence for three independently chosen endpoint slopes and disposes of all constant rows in the strict balanced setting.
author: mp_r250_joint_indexed_cover
proof:
Write \(f(w)=v\cdot w+c\).  Affineness gives the exact identity
\[
2f\left(\frac{x_0+x_2}{2}\right)=f(x_0)+f(x_2).
\tag{8}
\]
Assume first that \(f\) is nonconstant, so \(v\ne0\).  For any \(\sigma\in\mathbb R\), define
\[
U_\sigma=A_0\cap\{f\le\sigma\},\qquad
V_\sigma=A_2\cap\{f\le-\sigma\}.
\]
If \(x_0\notin U_\sigma\) and \(x_2\notin V_\sigma\), then
\[
f(x_0)>\sigma,\qquad f(x_2)>-\sigma,
\]
and hence (8) gives \(f((x_0+x_2)/2)>0\).  Such a pair is not in \(E_f\).  Therefore
\[
E_f\subseteq(U_\sigma\times A_2)\cup(A_0\times V_\sigma),
\]
so
\[
\tau(E_f)\le |U_\sigma|+|V_\sigma|.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(\sigma\) proves
\[
\tau(E_f)\le\kappa(f).
\tag{9}
\]

For the reverse inequality, let measurable \(U\subseteq A_0\) and \(V\subseteq A_2\) satisfy
\[
E_f\subseteq(U\times A_2)\cup(A_0\times V),
\tag{10}
\]
and put
\[
P=A_0\setminus U,\qquad Q=A_2\setminus V.
\]
Suppose first that \(P\ne\varnothing\) and \(Q\ne\varnothing\).  By (8) and (10),
\[
f(x_0)+f(x_2)\ge0
\qquad(x_0\in P,\ x_2\in Q).
\tag{11}
\]
The number
\[
\alpha=\inf_{x_0\in P}f(x_0)
\]
is finite because \(f\) is bounded on compact \(A_0\); it need not be attained.  If \(f(x_0)<\alpha\), then \(x_0\notin P\), so
\[
A_0\cap\{f<\alpha\}\subseteq U.
\tag{12}
\]
For any fixed \(x_2\in Q\), choose a sequence \(x_0^{(n)}\in P\) with
\[
f(x_0^{(n)})\longrightarrow\alpha.
\]
Equation (11) gives \(f(x_2)\ge-f(x_0^{(n)})\) for every \(n\), and passage to the limit gives
\[
f(x_2)\ge-\alpha.
\]
Hence
\[
A_2\cap\{f<-\alpha\}\subseteq V.
\tag{13}
\]
Every level set of the nonconstant affine function \(f\) is a line and has planar Lebesgue area zero.  Therefore (12)-(13) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
|U|+|V|
&\ge
\left|A_0\cap\{f<\alpha\}\right|
+
\left|A_2\cap\{f<-\alpha\}\right|\\
&=
\left|A_0\cap\{f\le\alpha\}\right|
+
\left|A_2\cap\{f\le-\alpha\}\right|\\
&\ge\kappa(f).
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]

It remains to check the two empty-complement cases in (10).  If \(P=\varnothing\), then \(U=A_0\) and \(|U|+|V|\ge a_0\).  Because \(f\) is bounded on both compact bodies, a sufficiently large positive \(\sigma\) makes \(U_\sigma=A_0\) and \(V_\sigma=\varnothing\).  Thus \(\kappa(f)\le a_0\), and again \(|U|+|V|\ge\kappa(f)\).  If \(Q=\varnothing\), a sufficiently large negative \(\sigma\) makes \(U_\sigma=\varnothing\) and \(V_\sigma=A_2\), so \(\kappa(f)\le a_2\le|U|+|V|\).  These cases include \(P=Q=\varnothing\).  Since every measurable cover (10) has cost at least \(\kappa(f)\), taking the infimum over all such covers gives
\[
\tau(E_f)\ge\kappa(f).
\tag{15}
\]
Together, (9) and (15) prove (1).  Notice that neither infimum was assumed to be attained.

Now let \(f\equiv c\).  If \(c<0\), then \(E_f=A_0\times A_2\).  For any vertex cover, its complements \(P,Q\) cannot both be nonempty, so every cover has cost at least \(m\); taking one whole side and the other side empty attains \(m\).  Hence \(\tau(E_f)=m\).  Also, for every \(\sigma\), at least one of
\[
c\le\sigma,\qquad c\le-\sigma
\]
holds, so at least one endpoint cap is its whole body.  Choosing \(\sigma<c\) gives the cost \(a_2\), while choosing \(\sigma>-c\) gives the cost \(a_0\).  Hence \(\kappa(f)=m\).

If \(c>0\), then \(E_f=\varnothing\), so \(\tau(E_f)=0\).  For any
\[
-c<\sigma<c,
\]
both endpoint caps are empty, so \(\kappa(f)=0\).

If \(c=0\), strictness in the definition of \(E_f\) again gives \(E_f=\varnothing\), hence \(\tau(E_f)=0\).  However, if \(\sigma<0\), the \(A_0\)-cap is empty and the \(A_2\)-cap is all of \(A_2\); if \(\sigma>0\), the \(A_0\)-cap is all of \(A_0\) and the \(A_2\)-cap is empty; and if \(\sigma=0\), both caps are whole.  Thus \(\kappa(f)=m\).  This proves the complete table (2), including the strict-open versus closed-cap boundary discrepancy at \(f\equiv0\).

We next prove (3).  If
\[
\max_i\bigl(b_i+\kappa(f_i)\bigr)\ge L,
\]
choose an index \(i\) attaining this finite maximum.  For every \(\sigma_i\),
\[
R_i(\sigma_i)\ge b_i+\kappa(f_i)\ge L.
\]
Therefore every independently chosen triple of slopes satisfies
\(\max_iR_i(\sigma_i)\ge L\).

Conversely, suppose
\[
b_i+\kappa(f_i)<L\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\tag{16}
\]
For each index separately, the definition of the infimum supplies a finite \(\sigma_i\) such that
\[
\left|A_0\cap\{f_i-\sigma_i\le0\}\right|
+
\left|A_2\cap\{f_i+\sigma_i\le0\}\right|
<L-b_i.
\tag{17}
\]
The three choices can be made simultaneously because \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\) are independent variables.  Equations (16)-(17) give
\[
R_i(\sigma_i)<L\qquad(i=1,2,3),
\]
so the universal row inequality fails.  This proves the converse by contraposition and establishes (3), whether or not any one-row infimum is attained.

Finally assume (4).  If \(M=\max\{a_0,a_2\}\), the strict inequality \(M<T/2\) is equivalent to
\[
M<a_1+m,
\]
and hence
\[
a_1+m>\frac{M+a_1+m}{2}=\frac T2.
\tag{18}
\]
For a constant \(f_i\equiv c\le0\), one has \(B_i=A_1\), and (2) shows that its endpoint contribution is always at least \(m\).  Equations (18) and \(T/2>2T/9\) prove (5), covering both negative and zero constants.

For a positive constant, \(B_i=\varnothing\), and (2) gives (6).  Thus a positive constant row contributes the same zero value to both sides of the criterion in (3), while every nonpositive constant row has already proved the target.  In the only remaining case, \(\kappa(f_i)=\tau(E_{f_i})\) for all three indices, so substituting (1)-(2) into (3) proves (7).
statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional convex bodies of positive areas \(a_0,a_2\), and put \(m=\min\{a_0,a_2\}\).  For an affine function \(f:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\), define
\[
E_f=
\left\{(x_0,x_2)\in A_0\times A_2:
f\left(\frac{x_0+x_2}{2}\right)<0\right\},
\]
\[
\tau(E_f)=
\inf\left\{
|U|+|V|:
\begin{array}{l}
U\subseteq A_0,\ V\subseteq A_2\text{ are measurable},\\
E_f\subseteq(U\times A_2)\cup(A_0\times V)
\end{array}
\right\},
\]
and
\[
\kappa(f)=
\inf_{\sigma\in\mathbb R}
\left(
\left|A_0\cap\{f-\sigma\le0\}\right|
+
\left|A_2\cap\{f+\sigma\le0\}\right|
\right).
\]
If \(f\) is nonconstant, then
\[
\tau(E_f)=\kappa(f).
\tag{1}
\]
For a constant \(f\equiv c\), the complete table is
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
&c<0&c=0&c>0\\ \hline
\tau(E_f)&m&0&0\\
\kappa(f)&m&m&0.
\end{array}
\tag{2}
\]
Thus (1) also holds for every nonzero constant, and \(f\equiv0\) is the unique exception.

Now let \(A_1\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a compact two-dimensional convex body of area \(a_1\).  Let \(f_1,f_2,f_3\) be affine with
\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1,
\]
put
\[
B_i=A_1\cap\{f_i\le0\},\qquad b_i=|B_i|,
\]
and, for independently chosen \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\in\mathbb R\), put
\[
R_i(\sigma_i)=
b_i+
\left|A_0\cap\{f_i-\sigma_i\le0\}\right|
+
\left|A_2\cap\{f_i+\sigma_i\le0\}\right|.
\]
For every real \(L\),
\[
\left[
\forall(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)\in\mathbb R^3,\quad
\max_i R_i(\sigma_i)\ge L
\right]
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\max_i\bigl(b_i+\kappa(f_i)\bigr)\ge L.
\tag{3}
\]

In the strict balanced setting
\[
a_j<\frac{T}{2}\quad(j=0,1,2),
\qquad T=a_0+a_1+a_2,
\qquad L=\frac{2T}{9},
\tag{4}
\]
every constant row is settled exactly as follows.

If \(f_i\equiv c\le0\), then
\[
R_i(\sigma)\ge a_1+m>\frac{T}{2}>\frac{2T}{9}
\qquad(\sigma\in\mathbb R),
\tag{5}
\]
so the universal row inequality already holds.  If \(f_i\equiv c>0\), then
\[
b_i=\kappa(f_i)=\tau(E_{f_i})=0,
\tag{6}
\]
and that row can be made empty by any \(-c<\sigma<c\).  Consequently, unless a nonpositive constant row has already proved the target, every row satisfies \(\kappa(f_i)=\tau(E_{f_i})\), and (3) becomes the exact equivalence
\[
\left[
\forall(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)\in\mathbb R^3,\quad
\max_i R_i(\sigma_i)\ge\frac{2T}{9}
\right]
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\max_i\left(b_i+\tau(E_{f_i})\right)\ge\frac{2T}{9}.
\tag{7}
\]
